Finally, simulation results compared the proposed modulation with classic carrier-based modulation and validated its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Fault Tolerant Control for Medium Voltage Hybrid MMC With Cold Reserve Submodules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: The hybrid modular multilevel converter (HMMC), which consists of half-and full-bridge sub modules (SMs), offers critical advantages in handling overmodulation conditions and blocking dc fault current compared to half-bridge MMC. The high number of SMs poses a threat to the proper operation of the HMMC after an SM failure. To ensure the reliability of HMMC, the use of redundant SMs is pivotal, particularly in medium-voltage applications where the number of SMs is comparatively lower than in high-voltage ones. The redundant SM can be used as a cold reserve SM, referring to the condition that the redundant SM is not being used in the normal condition and inserted after SM failure, which prevents an increase in MMC losses and components thermal stress. This work proposes a sorting method for the seamless and smooth insertion of the cold reserve SM in the event of SM failure, as a replacement for faulty SM. The main goal is to avoid the inrush current and high stress on the capacitor during the insertion of cold reserve SM and achieve a controlled charging process of the capacitor in the inserted SM. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the suggested method are validated through comprehensive simulation studies.

articleTitle: Grid-Forming Converter with Improved Dynamic and Disturbance Rejection Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: This paper proposes a control strategy for grid-forming converter based on a cascaded control scheme with current and voltage controllers. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the possibility of obtaining almost zero steady-state error for the current loop utilizing only a proportional controller with a magnitude and lead compensation functions to achieve high bandwidth. For the voltage loop, a disturbance input decoupling function is proposed to obtain better dynamic response for the converter under load changes. Simulations results prove the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: A Current-Limiting Direct Voltage Model Predictive Control for DC-DC Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: In this paper, a current-limiting-based direct voltage model predictive control (DVMPC) strategy is presented for controlling DC-DC boost converters, aimed at preventing over-current conditions and ensuring system stability across various operating modes. To achieve this, a discretized dynamic model that covers all feasible operating modes is developed to serve as the prediction model. An optimization scheme is then introduced to simultaneously regulate the output voltage and limit the inductor current, incorporating an adaptive current-limiting term into the conventional DVMPC cost function. Furthermore, the move blocking strategy is employed to adapt the strategy for real-time applications by reducing computational requirements, thereby improving its practical applicability. Extensive simulation analysis demonstrates the efficacy of the proposed method in safeguarding against component damage due to over-current and enhancing system stability across a wider range of power outputs.

articleTitle: Graph Neural Network Based Deep Reinforcement Learning for Volt - Var Control in Distribution Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: Voltage reactive power control (VVC) plays a vital role in future-oriented smart grids, which not only ensures the stable operation of the power system but also optimizes energy distribution and consumption. However, with the widespread access to distributed renewable power generation resources, the structure and operation mode of the power grid, especially the distribution network, are becoming more and more complex. The traditional VV C method is difficult to cope with this new situation due to its inherent limitations. challenge. These limitations include, but are not limited to, the static nature of the control strategy, lack of adaptability to dynamic changes in the grid, and computational inefficiency when dealing with large-scale networks. With the widespread use of artificial intelligence in smart grids, some deep-reinforcement learning algorithms have been used to solve this problem. However, because the algorithm is not good enough for controlling complex environments, in order to overcome these challenges, this paper proposes innovative methods based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and graph neural networks (GNN). GNN is used to extract graphical representations from topological maps of power systems and is trained with data from the VVC environment. Improve the efficiency and reliability of VV C by improving algorithms and optimization strategies.

articleTitle: An Active Power Decoupling Strategy to Reduce the Capacitor Size of a Cascaded H-Bridge Converter in a Solid State Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: This paper presents a control strategy for active power decoupling in a Solid State Transformer (SST) using a cascaded H-bridge (CHB) converter, dual active bridge (DAB) converters, and a high-frequency link (HFL). The strategy balances capacitor voltage and decouples power flow, significantly reducing second harmonic voltage ripple in DC link capacitors and potentially reducing their size.

articleTitle: Application of Statistical Model Checking for Robustness Comparison of Power Electronics Controllers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: Power electronic-based systems exhibit non-linear dynamics requiring simultaneous control of multiple control objectives. It is therefore expected that controllers that can cope with those nonlinearities will have a better performance than controllers requiring system linearization or nesting of the control objectives in a cascaded structure. However, the problem remains how to quantify their robustness and make a fair comparison between different non-linear controllers. The conventional tools used for the robustness validation of linear controllers cannot directly be applied to different non-linear controllers. Therefore, this paper demonstrates an approach based on statistical model checking for performing controller comparisons. The performance and robustness of different controllers (linear, model predictive, and neural networks-based) were compared in the same stochastic environment. Using this approach, a statistical estimate can be obtained for how the controller performance will be affected under different scenarios.

articleTitle: Realization of Real-Time Simulation of Power Electronics Systems in Applications - A Review of Requirements and Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: Power electronics systems consist of two or more power electronics basic circuits. Common are combinations of a rectifier and at least one DC/DC converter, however topologies with several DC/DC converters for creating different voltage levels are a usual approach for certain applications. Different control strategies exist for these systems, either dedicated controls for each device or a single control for multiple devices at a time. This paper describes how these systems, regardless of their control strategy, can be modeled to run in a real-time simulation. Large or complex systems need to be split into individual models which are then simulated on individual hardware platforms. The required communication between the models and the hardware platforms to run the models synchronously is included as well. Simulation results prove that this approach works well.

articleTitle: Emerging Trends and Challenges in Smart Power Distribution for Marine Transportation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: The maritime industry is experiencing a shift towards electrification of the propulsion system. This paper investigates the emerging trends and challenges in smart power distribution designed for marine propulsion, focusing on all-electric ships (AES) and hybrid energy systems. The typical components of the AES, such as generators, Energy storage systems (ESS), power system architecture, etc., are explored. The operational challenges in onboard ship power distribution and integration of shore microgrid with AES are presented. Advanced computing techniques and technology advancements in AES bring new challenges like optimization and cybersecurity. These challenges are further discussed in view of power quality and management.

articleTitle: A Simple Global Maximum Power Point Tracking Scheme With Region Segmentation for Partially Shaded PV Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: To reduce the levelized cost of photovoltaic (PV) en-ergy, traditional global maximum power point tracking (GMPPT) schemes are more and more employing sophisticated scanning or artificial intelligence technologies to optimize energy harvesting under partial shading conditions (PSCs). This may affect the convergence speed and implementation simplicity. To address these issues, a simple GMPPT scheme is proposed with a region- dependent segmentation (RDS) strategy. With the proposed scheme, locating the global maximum power point (GMPP) is efficiently accelerated. Compared with the conventional methods, a redundant scanning process is avoided due to the use of a low- complexity estimation of the GMPP voltage. Thus, the dynamics under PSCs can be improved. Simulations and experimental tests are carried out to validate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme under diverse shading scenarios.

articleTitle: Partial Inertial Support for PV MPPT Systems Connected to Grid Using the IPLL Control Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: Reduction of inertia from conventional generation is rising questions towards grid-operators about the reliability of generations in the upcoming years. The loss of synchronous generators in addition to the massive increase of renewable energy integration, especially on PV and wind, is creating some uncertainties about the stable operation of the electrical network. With this reduction of synchronous generation support, the rate of change of frequency is increasing during grid faults, giving rise to some protections tripping and creating a cascaded effect creating partial or total blackouts of the grid. In order to address this issue, this paper focuses on providing a stable partial inertial support for PV applications working on the maximum power point (MPP) to dynamically support the electrical grid.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Grid-Forming Inertial Response for Power Reference and Grid-Supporting Functionalities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: This article probes into the capability of the power control loop of a voltage source converter based on electromechanical behavior to reproduce the power injected into the grid with inertial characteristics, similar to a synchronous generator. It focuses on studying the behavior of the electromechanical loop within a range of values for the inertia constant and damping coefficient. The transfer function of the plant or converter has been compared with the transfer function of a second-order system to determine the typical parameters of these functions. Finally, the overshoot control capability has been validated as the natural frequency of the system through simulations and experimental tests. This validates the correlation between damping and the rise or fall slope of power in response to a step input. Additionally, the relationship between inertia and damping values with overshoot and settling time is validated.

articleTitle: Development of a Two-Level, Four-Leg Smart Inverter for Microgrid Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: Microgrids are growing at a rapid pace, and as a result, power electronic inverters are more necessary than ever. However, the development of an adaptable inverter based on a changing control objective that also contains grid-related functions is lacking. This paper investigates the development of a novel two-level, four-leg smart inverter for a microgrid that can solve this problem. First, the inverter topology is discussed, modeled, and controlled using a standard dual-loop voltage control. Second, grid-forming functions are investigated. Third, an additional layout and control system are created for the grid-following inverter. Fourth, a simulation is constructed, and the capabilities of the smart inverter are highlighted.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of a Grid-Forming Converter Without an Inner Current Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: This study presents a simple grid-forming control structure without any inner current control. A three-phase, two-level grid-connected converter with an LCL filter is the subject of the investigation. Detailed small-signal models are utilized to assess the system stability and to determine suitable control parameters. The expected system characteristics are verified with averaged and switched models as well as experimental data. When compared to conventional droop control with cascaded voltage and current control, the control scheme shows faster dynamic behavior, a wider stability range for high grid impedances, e.g., in strong grids, but requires a careful calibration of the droop parameters to balance between response time, stability, and the system's ability to dampen oscillations effectively.

articleTitle: Development of GaN - bases three-phase Grid- Tie Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: Wide band gap (WBG) semiconductor devices have been widely concerned due to their superior performance over conventional Si power devices. They are expected to improve the power converters' efficiency and density. The main objective of this paper is to present the design of a three-phase Ga-based inverter with a particular focus on the feasibility of GaN applications in PV inverters, reliability, and efficiency. PCB boards are designed and tested for the control and power circuits, and the advantage of fibre optic connection for the PWM transmission is highlighted. The methodology covers the main steps of PV inverter design and design considerations. The key parameters and experimental results are presented. The power density is 60 W/inch3, and the peak efficiency is 96% at 5kWload.

articleTitle: An Improved Distributed Economic Control Strategy in Combination with Unitized Regenerative Fuel Cell Stack
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: Hydrogen energy storage is characterized by high energy density and high capacity. Unitized regenerative fuel cell (URFC) stack is a more integrated hydrogen storage system but is still less reported in distributed DC microgrids. Its combination with electrical energy storage has a large potential in island microgrid applications. Economic dispatch (ED) is an important issue for islanded microgrids composed of distributed generation units (DGs) with different generation costs and capacities. In this paper, an improved distributed economic control strategy capable of voltage restoration is proposed to improve DC microgrid reliability and power quality. The proposed method is based on the incremental cost (IC) consensus distributed algorithm, which equals the theory that the lowest cost of the whole system can be obtained only if the IC of all the generating units is equal. In addition, one of the nodes is designed for high-quality voltage recovery. Power capacity constraints also need to be considered. Thus, in the proposed method, the node used to realize the voltage recovery can transfer the function to other power sources after reaching the capacity constraint; while the other nodes can be directly excised from the communication network. The simulation model and control strategies are implemented in Simulink software for validation.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Influence of the Dead-Time on the Performance of an LLC Resonant Converter for High-Power Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: In this paper, analytical equations are provided to model how dead-time influences the current efforts of an LLC resonant converter used as a DC transformer. The analytical equations to calculate the average and root mean square (rms) currents on the main devices of the converter in terms of dead-time are obtained. Thus, the dependency of the power losses and efficiency of the converter on the dead-time is described. Experimental results of a down-scale laboratory prototype of an LLC resonant converter rated at 750 V / 5 kW validate the theoretical study. The converter has attained an efficiency of 98.05% for a dead-time equals to 500 ns.

articleTitle: Challenges of Microgrid Stability Assessment in the Presence of Inverter-Based Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: Power electronics converters play a pivotal role in seamlessly integrating renewable energy sources into the grid. Microgrids, comprising distributed renewable sources, serve as local power hubs while facilitating surplus energy transfer to the main grid. The dynamic behavior of these power converters significantly influences microgrid stability. This paper investigates a microgrid system comprising PV inverters, passive loads, a static var compensator (SVC), and a dedicated grid-forming inverter designed for grid support. It is observed that upon reaching a certain number of PV inverters, the system may exhibit instability, which is highly related to the SVC. Such instability can be mitigated by the dedicated grid-forming inverter. Furthermore, the presence of instability indicates right-half-plane (RHP) poles in the grid subsystem impedance, posing challenges for impedance-based stability analysis and necessitating careful consideration.

articleTitle: A Novel Regulated High-Frequency DC Transformer for Intermediate Bus Architecture Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: In this paper, a novel high-frequency DC transformer (DCX) converter with regulating capacity is proposed for intermediate bus architecture (IBA). The proposed scheme is composed by a dual-output DCX stage and a non-isolated dc-dc stage, where the DCX stage takes most of the power conversion and the dc-dc stage takes the voltage regulation duty. Compared with the conventional two-stage DCX solution, the proposed scheme has the advantages of higher efficiency, non-isolation control and higher system reliability. Meanwhile, it is flexible to meet the requirements of different voltage regulation range for intermediate bus converters (IBCs) by regulating the power distribution ratio. The operation principles and the design consideration of the proposed regulated DCX are analyzed in detail. Finally, a 12V/200W-output prototype is developed with different power distribution ratios, which proves the superiorities of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Real-Time Cosimulation of Power Systems: Integration of eMEGASIM and ePHASORSIM Using OPAL-RT Simulators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: This article presents a real-time cosimulation between two OPAL-RT simulators, utilizing the eMEGAsim system for simulations in the time domain and the ePHASORsim system for simulations in the phasor domain. It focuses on simulating a distributed Virtual Synchronous Generator control system with real power converters connected to a power system, facilitated by the interface through a high-speed DOLPHIN communication cable. The control system and interface configuration for cosimulation are detailed, along with the results obtained from the simulations. This real-time cosimulation approach provides an effective tool for the analysis and development of control systems in power environments.

articleTitle: Forecasting hybrid renewable power generation in Luxembourg: a comparative study of convolutional neural network's application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: Access to reliable renewable power generation forecasting tools is crucial for optimizing grid operations and advancing the integration of renewable energy, which in turn leads to the sustainability of energy systems. This study develops a forecasting model utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for precise prediction of hybrid solar and wind power generation in Luxembourg. Through a comprehensive comparative analysis exploring various combinations of critical hyperparameters, we demonstrate the significant capability of the CNN approach to serve as an effective prediction tool for hybrid renewable energy production. Our findings underscore the reliable potential of CNNs to enhance the accuracy of renewable energy forecasts, thereby enabling a more seamless and efficient integration of renewable energy sources into Luxembourg's power grid. Our CNN model demonstrated exceptional performance, with an R-squared (R2) exceeding 90%, particularly for forecasting horizons of 5, and 24 hours ahead.

articleTitle: Power Fluctuation Suppression in Energy Storage for PV-Battery GFM Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: Grid-forming (GFM) control is increasingly adopted in grid-connected inverters for frequency support, as a promising solution for the large-scale integration of renewable energy resources, like solar photovoltaic (PV). To solve the uncertainty of the PV power and reserve extra energy for frequency support, a battery energy storage system (BESS) is usually adopted. However, in the PV-battery GFM system, as the PV system and the BESS are coupled at the DC bus, any power fluctuation in the PV system will directly influence the BESS, which contributes to a reduction in the lifespan of batteries. The BESS power fluctuation in this process remains unclear. As such, in this paper, the typical control of the PV-battery GFM system is analyzed in order to explore the interaction between the BESS and the PV system. A control strategy is presented to suppress the PV power fluctuation and improve the DC-link voltage dynamic of the BESS. And, the control parameters are designed for the presented control strategy. Experimental tests have demonstrated the effectiveness of the control scheme.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Bond Wire Degradation in Power Modules During DC and AC Power Cycling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: This study assesses bond wire degradation differences between DC and AC power cycling tests in IGBT power modules. With existing experimental data, an empirical lifetime model has been developed for both methods. With the bond wire lift-off being the main failure mechanism, physical modeling approach is applied using a simplified thermo-mechanical finite element model to examine the temperature evolution, stress and strain development at the bond wire-chip interface. Factors including heating time, temperature gradient, and current density are addressed and discussed to explain the number of cycles to failure difference between the two power cycling test methods.

articleTitle: Harmonic Forecasting in Power Electronics: AI-Driven Machine Learning Modeling Approach for Voltage Source Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: This research compares neural network methods in predicting Voltage Source Converters' (VSCs) harmonic characteristics, essential for power electronics performance and grid compatibility. A model is developed using both time and frequency-domain data. Two approaches are used: training on time-domain data and converting it to frequency-domain before training. Results offer insights into VSC harmonic prediction techniques and enhance understanding of VSC harmonic analy-sis.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Strategy for Grid Forming Control in DC Coupled Photovoltaic and Battery Energy Storage Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: This paper presents an integrated DC-DC and DCAC grid-forming control strategy for DC-coupled photovoltaic (PV) plus battery energy storage systems, considering the effect of DC link voltage variations caused by direct PV connections. A power reference algorithm determines power distribution between the PV and battery to the grid while observing device power ratings to prevent the over-rating of components and keep the battery's state of charge within an acceptable range. The simulated utility-scale model in MATLAB/Simulink illustrates its ability against extreme phase angle variation contingencies in the grid while controlled through grid-forming control with a fast dynamic on DC link voltage. The simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed control in integrating PV plus battery configurations with grid forming control and maintaining reliable grid operation under severe grid disturbances.

articleTitle: Impedance Estimation for Transient Stability Enhancement of Virtual Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: In this paper, a passive technique for estimating the impedance and voltage of a Thévenin grid is presented. The method can be applied when either the maximum active power or minimum reactive power operating point, with respect to the power angle, is crossed. This work addresses transient events, for which the former occurs. A key assumption is that the power response of the converter is sufficiently slow such that the steady-state equations for active and reactive power remain accurate as the power angle varies, which is valid for virtual synchronous machines. In conjunction with the equal-area criterion, the estimated parameters are used to appropriately adjust the reference active power to maintain synchronism with the grid. The methodology is validated in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Adaptive Control for Enhanced Performance in Grid-Connected Agricultural Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: This paper investigates the non-linear behavior of a unidirectional Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC)-based DC-DC converter, specifically designed for grid-connected agricul-tural machines, to ensure an efficient, reliable power supply and highly dynamic peak power capabilities. Based on the insights gained, an adaptive voltage control strategy is proposed to improve the dynamic response performance of the converter across its entire operational range. The proposed strategy is validated through simulation results.

articleTitle: The Matrix Hybrid Solid State Transformer: Leveraging Three Phase Systems for Enhanced Grid Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: Hybrid Solid State Transformers (HSSTs) are systems comprising of a fractional power solid-state transformer (SST) integrated with a standard full power line frequency transformer (LFT). HSSTs serve as an optimum compromise between the cost effectiveness and resiliency of the LFT and the controllability and responsiveness of the SST. Previous works [2] [3] have studied the concept of a single-phase HSST using single-stage SST units. This paper discusses the prospect of expanding the concept to three-phase systems and exploring the additional control capabilities that it offers. The proposed system offers a control range akin to Unified Power Flow Controllers whilst using single stage isolated AC-AC topologies.

articleTitle: Decoupled Robust Backstepping Control of Multiphase Interleaving Converters for Power-to-Hydrogen Systems in DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: In this paper, the control of a PV-battery-based DC microgrid is studied for powering the electrolyzer. Three-phase interleaving topology is implemented for three different converters, boost, four switches single inductor buck-boost (FSIB), and buck respectively. The MPPT and droop-based control is advised for maximum power extraction and DC bus voltage regulation. Finally, a backstepping-based robust nonlinear controller is developed for current and voltage control. The proposed controller aims to provide a solution for two control problems of the interleaving converter, smooth power sharing between different phases of each power converter, and fine tracking of the desired reference. The systematic control design approach also prevents the use of multiple PI loops. Moreover, it provides a large signal stability analysis of the system using Lyapunov theory under different load scenarios. The proposed algorithm is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink to verify the results through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Analysis of Power Quality Improvement Techniques Applied to Grid-connected Wind Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: In the current transition of power industry from non-renewable generation toward renewable-based generation, wind energy is experiencing the highest penetration among the other renewable sources. Owing to low cost and abundant availability, wind energy generation has become a promising option to address the demand of cheap and clean energy. However, the integration of diverse type of Wind Power Plants (WPP) to the existing utility grids may bring forward multiple Power Quality (PQ) challenges such as harmonics, voltage sag/swell, voltage and power imbalances, low power factor, to name but a few. To address these issues researchers have proposed various PQ compensating devices over the years which have been updated in direct proportion to fast growing advancement in the design, control and operation of wind integrated power systems. This paper essentially aims to explain and classify different PQ issues and proposed improvement techniques on the bases of their applications, configurations, capabilities, advantages, and implementation cost in detail, which can provide a base information to the researchers working in this field. Moreover, simulations have been performed to demonstrate the performance of STATCOM in enhancing the voltage of grid-connected wind power plants.

articleTitle: Hybrid Control for Integrating Grid-Forming and Grid-Following Capabilities in a Single VSI: An Efficiency-Driven Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel hybrid control (HC) scheme, seamlessly integrating grid-forming and grid-following capabilities within a single voltage source inverter (VSI). HC enables a single VSI to effectively replicate the functions of two virtual parallel VSIs operating independently as grid-forming and grid-following inverters while ensuring system stability and reliability. This enhances VSI effectiveness, allowing simultaneous execution of vital tasks including voltage and frequency regulation, grid support, and precise reference power tracking. An HC-equipped VSI can emulate virtual inertia, ensuring stable voltage and frequency under various operational conditions with rapid and desirable dynamic responses. Furthermore, for optimal coordination with auxiliary control layers, the secondary control layer, responsible for overseeing grid frequency and voltage amplitude restoration, seamlessly integrates with the HC-based primary control. This integration ensures the effective operation of an HC-enabled VSI within a hierarchical control structure. The effectiveness of the proposed control scheme is substantiated via comprehensive simulation studies conducted on an HC-enabled multi-inverter system operating in islanded mode.

articleTitle: Last Developments and New Technologies in Solid-State Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: The solid-state transformer (SST) technology has been greatly involved in recent decades due to new semiconduc-tor technology, extensive efforts to improve magnetic designs, and intensive research on optimizing power converter designs. Moreover, new applications and trends for SSTs have emerged. The purpose of this paper is to highlight the latest developments in the field of SSTs, starting from the system level, which includes power converter topologies and architectures, to the level of individual components, such as power semiconductor technology and magnetic components. The main power converter architectures of SST and their design challenges have been analyzed, as well as the design of high-power, high-isolation medium frequency transformers for SST.

articleTitle: Automation Framework for Blockchain-Based Coordination of Distributed Energy Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: Blockchain technology represents a secure distributed alternative to central architectures, as this technology can allow a democratic distribution of power where actors with mixed or even opposite interests can contribute to a common objective by aggregated effort. Nonetheless, the lack of working frameworks nor consideration for legacy solutions for preexisting devices limits the technology adoption on a higher scale. In the present paper, different components necessary to define an automation solution are discussed, as the blockchain architecture, the different standards involved on every automation levels (i.e. IEC61970, IEC60870, and IEC61850), their integration, and the necessary tools to tackle the particular cases in a broader perspective. Finally, the current work tests the proposed framework in a simulated network, presenting the hardware and software requirements, to close the work discussing the impact of the results considering the possible applications as might be the case of monitoring, control, or protection algorithms.

articleTitle: Optimal Re-Dispatch and Reactive Power Management in the Fuerteventura-Lanzarote Grid Using Real-Time Optimization in the Loop
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: This paper proposes a loop-based optimization framework for reactive power management and re-dispatch driven by the exceeding of technical constraints. The proposed setup calculates and updates the setpoints of power plant controllers in real time while minimizing power losses and re-dispatch costs and ensuring a stable operation in steady-state. For this purpose, we introduce RTOLab, Real-Time Optimization Laboratory, a real-time (RT) Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) simulation setup designed to test and validate grid management strategies based on real-time optimization in the loop. RTOLab enables the analysis of the interaction between high-level management strategies, which are based on optimization algorithms, and low-level controls pertaining to each asset of the grid. Drawing on the capabilities of RTOLab, this paper explores the reactive power sharing problem by proposing a centralized strategy. This scheme prioritizes minimizing both active power losses and re-dispatch costs updating the active power setpoints of an Energy Management System (EMS) or market clearing result. The performance of the proposed framework is analyzed through a one-hour simulation in the isolated grid of Fuerteventura-Lanzarote islands in the canary archipelago.

articleTitle: An Optimal Power-Splitting Strategy for Hybrid Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: The wide deployment of inverter-based resources is changing the grid characteristics and demanding rapid changes in the control and operation of power grids. Storage is becoming a key component of this transition, as it can provide a wide palette of services, from fast frequency response to congestion management. This implies a broad range of requirements for the storage units, in terms of energy, power, response times, etc. Hybrid storage systems, combining units with different properties, such as supercapacitors, high-energy or high-power batteries, represent a natural choice that can cover many grid services. These services do not only require active power but also reactive power, and ideally they will be provided by the storage system while optimizing its overall efficiency. In this work we formally derive active and reactive power splitting strategies that minimize the operation losses among all inverters of the hybrid storage system. These strategies are computationally light and do not rely on complex optimizers, thereby facilitating their implementation in embedded systems. A realistic example depicts the clear improvement of this approach against simple power splitting strategies. While our focus lies on hybrid storage systems, the formulation can be applied as well to hybrid power plants, since their power losses can be characterized by similar mathematical functions.

articleTitle: Grid-Forming Photovoltaic Generators Operating During Power System Transients
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: Grid-forming (GF) converters based on renewable energy sources are a fundamental piece of future power systems. In particular, the design specifications of GF converters in photovoltaic (PV) applications are difficult to meet because PV inverters lack energy storage. The operation of GF-PV inverters under normal conditions has already been addressed in the existing literature. However, the operation in case of large disturbances, such as faults, has rarely been explored. In this paper, a GF controller for a two-stage PV inverter that is robust against faults is presented. This control system includes several improvements compared to the traditional GF controller. Power feedforwards and saturations are applied to improve the transient performance. Also, a method to keep the virtual swing equation synchronised when the current saturates is presented. Remarkably, there is no need to change the controller structure during faults. Simulations of a PV inverter connected to a simple power system based on a diesel generator and loads are conducted. The results show that the proposed countermeasures improve the performance of GF-PV inverters in case of faults. In addition, it is shown that keeping the phase of the virtual swing equation and the grid voltage space vector synchronised is important to avoid the collapse of the dc-link voltage. Suggestions for further research are presented in the last part of the work.

articleTitle: Discussion on Voltage Regulation Alternatives in Distribution Networks with Massive Distributed Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: Environmental and sustainability concerns have ca used a significant surge in distributed energy resources (DER) penetration into the power grid. This may lead to voltage limit violations in the distribution grid, makingvoltage control more relevant than ever. Due to this fact, the search for voltage control alternatives at different levels of distribution systems has been an o bj ect of concern, considering tha t depending on the volta ge level and the DER penetration percentage, conventional solutions implemented are sometimes not feasible or ineffective. On the other hand, solutions implemented by the accessor can limit the DER generation capacity. This work presents the results of a discussion on solutions used for voltage control in low and medium-voltage electrical networks with massive integration of renewable distributed generation. Additionally, simulation results in PSCAD/EMTDC are presented with Direct Voltage Control (DVC) alternatives showing their dynamics response.

articleTitle: A Methodology for Analysis and Design of Dispatchable Virtual Oscillator Grid-Forming Control Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: This article proposes a methodology for analyzing and designing Andronov-Hopf (AH) dispatchable virtual oscillators (dVOC) Grid-Forming (GFM) control methods. With the proposed methodology, four existing dVOC methods are reassessed and new insights on their structures are provided. Furthermore, a unified parameterization procedure is developed so that the inverter's steady-state behavior follows a prescribed droop behavior. Controller-Hardware-in-Loop results show that when applying the proposed parameterization with the same droop objectives, the analyzed dVOC methods presented, on one hand, similar dynamic behavior responses and the other hand, different steady-state droop behaviors. The proposed methodology may also be used to design AH dVOC GFM control methods, where main design criteria is the specification of output droop behavior of the grid-forming inverter.

articleTitle: Overview of Various Carbon Neutral Energy Storage Solutions, Supporting Grid Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: Renewable energy systems have gained popularity in recent years due to its well-proven technology. One of the most important challenges with intermittent energy is stability during periods of low grid activity. This paper describes the importance of stability aspect of a grid, having dominating feed from variable renewable energy sources. Renewable energy sources, however, carry uncertainty, with intermittence and non-controllability of wind and solar energy. Research and innovations over the years have successfully introduced various control strategies and optimization methods for tackling with those limitations. Various environment-friendly energy storage systems are briefly discussed in this paper, together with their merits and limitations.

articleTitle: Reliable Decentralized Control Scheme of DC Microgrid Using Transition Operations Under DC-Link Voltage Sensor Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: This paper proposes a power flow control strategy (PFCS) for a decentralized DC microgrid (DCMG) system using transition operations based on the DC-link voltage (DCV) observer value to achieve both the voltage and power regulations even under DCV sensor faults. The transition operation modes are employed to transmit the information of the DCMG system to other power agents without any digital communication links while the steady-state operation modes are used to ensure the DCV regulation to the nominal value. Moreover, to maintain the system stabilization even under DCV sensor faults, a voltage sensor fault identification method is introduced for each power agent in the decentralized DCMG by using the estimated DCV value. When a DCV sensor fault occurs in a power agent, its operation is adjusted to the proper control mode to ensure the DCMG system stabilization. Several simulations are carried out with the PSIM software to verify the reliability of the proposed PFCS.

articleTitle: An Optimized Electric Power and Reserves Economic Dispatch Algorithm for Isolated Systems Considering Water Inflow Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: While the share of renewable energy in intercon-nected systems has been increasing steadily, in isolated systems it represents a bigger challenge. This paper presents a dispatch algorithm integrating thermal, wind, solar and hydro generation and storage for an isolated network, which allows maximizing renewable energy integration and reducing the share of thermal energy in the mix. The possibility of using the battery to provide “spinning” reserve is also considered. The algorithm was tested and validated using real data from the island of Madeira, Portugal. Results prove the robustness and flexibility of the algorithm, showing that a significant decrease in the thermal fraction is achievable, and that it is possible to accommodate an increase in renewable generation with minimal or no curtailment at all.

articleTitle: Virtual Energy Storage Stacking in Day-Ahead and mFRR markets - A Spanish Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: Addressing the imperative for climate action requires adaptable energy solutions. Leveraging distributed tech-nology like Virtual Energy Storage Systems (VESSs), the i-STENTORE project aims to pioneer innovative solutions for the widespread deployment of energy storage systems. This paper explores the potential of VESSs to increase the revenue of different distributed renewable technologies in the Iberian Wholesale and manual Frequency Restoration Reserve (mFRR) markets. Research up to date has focused on several market integration aspect of VESSs, yet considering the intricancies of the Iberian market of these technologies remains unexplored. The research aims to provide real-world insights into the potential of VESSs to increase the revenue of these technologies by stacking different services in the Iberian market. The results will show the potential of this demonstrator to increase profits using the concept of VESS and several storage technologies into the Iberian market.

articleTitle: Synchronization Circuit Design for Battery Energy Storage Integration in DFIM-Based Hydro Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: Highly-rated variable speed pumped storage power plants (VSPSPPs) often utilize doubly fed induction machines (DFIM) with partially-rated megawatt (MW) power converters. This choice is driven by the machine's ability to deliver enhanced energy efficiency across a wide range of water head variations, while also offering cost savings and contributing to grid stability. In the DFIM, rotor excitation is managed by partially-rated power converters, which regulate the bulk excitation current. For instance, a standard 250MW DFIM typically handles 11,620 A of excitation current. A synchronization circuit for battery energy storage system (BESS) is an essential component that ensures the safe and stable integration of the BESS into the power grid. The circuit synchronizes the voltage and frequency of the BESS with the grid to prevent power fluctuations, stabilize the system, and avoid damage to electrical equipment. Sub synchronous oscillation (SSO) of a series compensated power system is said to be the cause of rotor shaft failure. In consideration of this issue, this paper analyses synchronization circuit using the BESS to stabilized power oscillations in transmission lines with series compensation and variable-speed hydroelectric units. In MATLAB Simulink, the efficacy of the proposed system with DFIM-based series compensated transmission line is validated. A practical demonstration of a synchronization circuit with BESS connected to DC-link of DFIM converter is carried out in the lab.

articleTitle: Modified Sorting Algorithm for Fault- Tolerant Operation of Hybrid MMC With Hot Reserve Submodules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: The hybrid modular multilevel converter (HMMC) is formed of a combination of half- and full-bridge submodules. HMMC offers advantages in working under overmodulation conditions and effectively blocking the dc fault current with a reduced number of semiconductor switches compared to FB-based MMC, which makes it a fitting option for high and medium-voltage applications. While the modular nature of the MMC is considered a key strength, a high number of power switches raises a potential reliability concern in the event of sub-module (SM) failure. Hence, the implementation of fault-tolerant strategies is critical to ensure the uninterrupted operation of the HMMC. This study aims to develop a fault-tolerant technique through hot reserve redundant SMs by using a modified sorting algorithm. The sorting algorithm is adopted to ensure the correct operation of HMMC during fault occurrence. Also, this work introduces a new control on the insertion index to operate in overmodulation operating mode with reduced dc-link voltage. Finally, the feasibility and availability of the modified sorting method for using hot reserve SMs in HMMC are verified through the EMT simulations in MATLAB\\\\\\\\Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Predicting Hydro Reservoir Inflows with AI Techniques using Radar Data and a Numerical Weather Prediction Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: Reducing the gap between renewable energy needs and supply is crucial to achieve sustainable growth. Hydroelectric power production predictions in several Madeira Island catchment regions are shown in this article using Long Short-Term Memory, LSTM, networks. In order to foresee hydro reservoirs inflows, our models take into account the island's dynamic precipitation and flow rates and simplify the process of water moving from the cloud to the turbine. The model developed for the Socorridos Fajã Rodrigues system demonstrates the proficiency of LSTMs in capturing the unexpected flow behavior through its low RMSE. When it comes to energy planning, the model built for the CTIII Paul Velho system gives useful information despite its lower accuracy when it comes to anticipating problems.

articleTitle: Open Battery Platform: Open-Source Power Electronic Devices for Renewable Generation and Energy Storage Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: The use of renewable energy sources, such as pho-tovoltaic (PV), and energy storages is growing rapidly. This, together with the emerging aspects of new battery technologies and the reuse of batteries from the mobility sector, increases the need for variable integration through power electronic components. Due to its global importance, a comprehensive system is necessary to overcome various challenges, such as the integration of different renewable energy sources, storage technologies and the need for local or grid connections. This paper presents a system concept and demonstrates the practical implementation of a battery storage system in combination with PV and a grid connection. For comparison purposes, a reference system was built using commercially available components, which were gradually replaced. All components were developed under the concept of open-source hardware and software. The monitoring and control of system components, remote monitoring, and reference data collection rely on open-source tools.

articleTitle: Operation Maps for Hybrid Electrolyser and Battery Systems - A Luxembourgish Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: The ever-increasing need for climate action mo-tivates the development of new and flexible energy solutions that adapts to society's modern energy requirements. The i-STENTORE project aims to pioneer innovative solutions for the widespread deployment of hybrid energy storage systems. This paper investigates the simultaneous provision of flexibility services and hydrogen production within a real-world Lux-embourgish hybrid energy system demonstrator, using multi-objective optimisation. While previous research has focused on either flexibility services or hydrogen production individually, this study fills the gap of a comparative analysis of different scenarios that consider trade-offs between these two objectives. The research provides operational insights into strategies for maximising economic viability and sustainability by analysing aspects such as the levelised cost of hydrogen, energy, degradation, and the impact of the battery size. The results show the potential of this demonstrator to provide flexibility to the system without significantly impacting in the hydrogen production.

articleTitle: Testing the Local Stability of a Multi-Machine Power System with Constant Power Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: With the widespread adoption of switched power converters within the power grid as both sources and sinks, the necessity arises for establishing verifiable stability conditions. We assume here that power sources can be modelled as synchronous generators - this encompasses virtual synchronous generators - while power sinks are operating as constant power loads. We provide a small-signal stability criterion for a model that uses time-varying phasors, characterized by a lossless transmission network and constant power loads distributed throughout the network. A key concept in this study is the matrix <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>, representing the partial derivatives of the generator powers with respect to their relative angles, computed at an equilibrium point. Our main result is that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H > 0$</tex> implies the local asymptotic stability of this equilibrium point. Moreover, the equilibrium point is unstable if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex> is full-rank and not positive definite. To demonstrate the practical significance of our theorem, we conduct a case study, highlighting its applicability in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: A Systematic Review of Solid-State Transformer for Large Ships and Their Shore Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Power Electronics for Distributed Generation Systems (PEDG)
abstract: In response to the emission reduction goals established by the International Maritime Organization, the push towards ship electrification introduces new challenges. This shift demands novel solutions in maritime technology, the development of infrastructure, and energy management strategies. Integrating DC-driven fuel cells and energy storage alongside generators constrained by fixed speeds due to AC usage requires employing low-voltage and/or medium-voltage DC distribution. Considering the importance, this paper explores the burgeoning field of SSTs and their pivotal role in maritime applications by providing a comprehensive analysis of shipboard microgrid (SMG) architectures, categorizing them based on distribution types and propulsion types. The paper thoroughly examines the potential realization of SSTs within these SMG power architectures. Additionally, it delves into the investigation of potential power architectures for shore power supply, considering the implementation of SSTs. In the context of shipboard protection systems, this paper outlines the distinct requirements for DC SMGs compared to terrestrial-based microgrids. To illustrate the operation of SSTs at a system level in maritime applications, the paper presents generic control frameworks for both single and multiple-networked SSTs.
